name: URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8
source_title: Requested CROSSINGTUD CrySL rule path was not found; official Android and Java sources for the underlying java.net.URLEncoder API were consulted
protocol: URLEncoder.encode(input, charsetName) where charsetName resolves to UTF-8; no object-lifecycle ordering is involved.
important_note: The convention-derived target type is java.net.URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8, whose simple name exactly matches the specification ID. Neither the requested canonical CrySL file nor the current JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src directory established that this type or rule is presently published. The representative finding nevertheless aligns with documented java.net.URLEncoder encoding-selection behavior. This is a compatibility rule, not proof of an exploitable security defect.

events.name: encode_with_named_charset
events.condition: Observing the event means a call resolving to URLEncoder.encode(String, String) is present. Its UTF-8 predicate is satisfied only when the effective second argument is evidenced to designate UTF-8; observing an encode call alone, or merely observing an unknown or nonconstant charset expression, does not establish that predicate.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that com.mde.potdroid.helpers.f.a necessarily contains a direct java.net.URLEncoder call; the representative finding supplies a detector message but not the method body or resolved call target.
Do not infer that java.net.URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8 is a physically shipped JDK or Android runtime class; its inclusion is convention-derived and its source linkage remains unverified.
Do not infer that ISO-8859-15 is unsupported on the executing platform or that the call must throw UnsupportedEncodingException.
Do not infer that non-UTF-8 form encoding is universally incorrect; an interoperating peer may explicitly require a legacy charset.
Do not infer encryption, authentication, integrity, URL validation, or generic RFC-3986 URI-component correctness from this rule.
Do not infer that the encoded value reaches a network request, HTML form, query string, or security-sensitive sink.
Do not infer that the detector accepts every UTF-8 alias or the Charset overload; the unavailable CrySL source is needed to establish its exact acceptance relation.
semantic_scope: A static compatibility check over a selected charset argument at an apparent java.net.URLEncoder form-encoding call. The representative message specifically reports the selected encoding, ISO-8859-15, as potentially incompatible with the UTF-8 recommendation for application/x-www-form-urlencoded data.

detector_semantics.claim: Using an encoding other than UTF-8 with URLEncoder may introduce interoperability incompatibilities.
predicates: A relevant URLEncoder encode call is resolved or syntactically recognized.
The encoding-selection argument is available to the analysis as a value such as ISO-8859-15.
That value is judged not to satisfy the detector's UTF-8 requirement.
limitations: The exact CrySL event declaration, accepted aliases, interprocedural value resolution, and treatment of unknown values could not be verified because the named CrySL source was unavailable.
The finding supplies no evidence about the consumer's expected charset, payload characters, actual runtime value, or whether encoded output is used.
The exact target type required by the CrySL naming convention could not be confirmed from the available CROSSINGTUD repository contents.

documented_behavior: java.net.URLEncoder converts strings to application/x-www-form-urlencoded form.
Alphanumeric characters and . - * _ are retained, spaces become +, and other characters are converted to bytes in the selected charset and percent-encoded.
The encode(String, String) overload looks up the charset by name; official Java and Android sources state that UTF-8 should be used and that another encoding may introduce incompatibilities.
preconditions: The input string and charset selection must be non-null for the documented overloads.
For encode(String, String), the charset name must identify a charset supported by the runtime or the call can throw UnsupportedEncodingException.
Interoperability requires the producer and consumer to agree on form encoding and character encoding.
unknowns: The Android API level and library implementation used by the analyzed application are not supplied.
It is not known whether the finding corresponds to encode(String, String), a wrapper around it, or a detector-specific modeled call.
It is not known whether the receiving service expects UTF-8, ISO-8859-15, or another protocol-specific encoding.

security_semantics.detector_claim: A non-UTF-8 encoding selection may produce incompatible application/x-www-form-urlencoded output.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: A compatibility failure occurs only when the encoding selected by the producer differs from the encoding expected by the consumer for data whose encoded byte representation differs between those charsets.

source_level: The exact URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8.crysl source, or an authoritative compiled-rule or metadata artifact that maps this specification ID to its governed qualified type.
The rule's explicit EVENTS and CONSTRAINTS clauses to establish accepted UTF-8 spellings, overload coverage, and unknown-value behavior.
Resolved source or bytecode for com.mde.potdroid.helpers.f.a to connect the representative finding to a concrete invocation.
runtime: The evaluated second argument passed to URLEncoder.encode at runtime.
The Android or JDK runtime version and installed charset support.
Evidence that the returned encoded string is consumed by the relevant downstream operation.
compatibility: The remote endpoint's or file format's declared expected encoding.
An end-to-end test containing non-ASCII characters that differ under UTF-8 and ISO-8859-15.
Evidence that application/x-www-form-urlencoded, rather than generic URI-component escaping, is the intended encoding format.

known_false_positive_shapes: The encoded input is restricted to ASCII characters, for which UTF-8 and ISO-8859-15 commonly yield the same bytes for relevant characters.
A legacy peer, server, or file format explicitly requires ISO-8859-15 and decodes the output using that same charset.
The encoded result is discarded, used only locally, or never reaches an interoperability boundary.
A UTF-8-compatible value is computed indirectly or supplied through a constant or alias that the detector cannot resolve.
The actual operation is not an HTML-form-compatible exchange, so the W3C form-encoding compatibility recommendation is not the applicable contract.
The detector reports a nonconstant or path-merged charset value even though every feasible runtime value used at the relevant sink is UTF-8; exact unknown-value handling is unverified.
unknowns: Whether URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8.crysl existed only in an older, forked, generated, or non-public ruleset.
The authoritative package of the required simple-name-exact governed type URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8; java.net.URLEncoder_EncodeUTF8 is a convention-derived attribution, not a verified runtime class.
Whether the detector governs only URLEncoder.encode(String, String), also governs encode(String, Charset), or models wrappers.
Whether UTF8, UTF_8, Charset.forName("UTF-8"), and StandardCharsets.UTF_8 satisfy the detector's intended predicate.
Whether the detector's message is emitted only for concrete disallowed encodings or also for unresolved or path-dependent charset values.
Whether the reported ISO-8859-15 call operates on user-visible non-ASCII data and interoperates with a UTF-8-expecting peer.
